name: Ironbridge cast-iron arch bridge
description: An iron arch supported a river crossing on masonry abutments, using cast members with additional wrought iron rather than an all-masonry superstructure.

date.basis: The cited source reports this year for the scoped event.

events.statement: The Coalbrookdale cast-iron bridge over the Severn was completed in 1779.

evidence.supports: The Coalbrookdale cast-iron bridge over the Severn was completed in 1779.
The source describes Coalbrookdale Company and this contribution.

earliest_record.rationale: Earliest sourced date for the specific documented case; this does not establish invention or worldwide priority.

caveats: Construction completion is not necessarily first public opening; iron and cost estimates concern this bridge as a whole.

research.note: Independently checked 1779 completion, cost greater than £6000, 300 tons and Coalbrookdale supply in Historic England. The reported personal contribution by Abraham Darby III awaits a registered person.

measures.money_context: Nominal total construction cost in late 1770s; source says over £6,000.
